name: Yallingup
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage 'Yallingup' page and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) town page; beachside village visitors base in for Ngilgi Cave, the beach and Injidup.
objection: Its draws (Ngilgi Cave, Yallingup Beach, Injidup Natural Spa, Canal Rocks) are separate candidates; listing the town beside them may be a wrapper (COVERAGE 'a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw').

name: Augusta
reason: Re-looked: counted sources found. Wikivoyage 'South West (Western Australia)' Cities list ('a wild bit of coastline with a famous lighthouse and waterwheel') and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Augusta town page and '10 Ways to Discover Augusta'. Town visitors base in for Cape Leeuwin, the Hardy Inlet and whale watching.
objection: No Wikivoyage article of its own (404); its headline draw, Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse, is a separate spot.

name: Pemberton
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage 'Pemberton (Western Australia)', westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) South West page ('town of towering timbers', Gloucester Tree) and southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) town page; base for the karri forests and climbing trees.
objection: Its draws (Gloucester Tree, Beedelup Falls, Bicentennial Tree) are separate spots.

name: Donnybrook
reason: Re-looked: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury Geographe page gives it a section (apple capital, Australia's biggest free-entry fun park, heritage architecture) and southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) lists it as a town. Two counted sources.
objection: A farming town most travellers pass through on the highway; its one named draw (the Apple Fun Park) is a playground.

name: Harvey
reason: Re-looked: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury Geographe page gives Harvey its own section (cheese, craft beer, wine, orange juice, Noongar/Italian heritage) and harveyregion.com.au (Shire tourism) covers it; shortlisted Top Tourism Town.
objection: Agricultural town with no single headline sight; visitors mostly stop briefly on the South Western Highway. Arguably review.

name: Bridgetown
reason: Re-looked: Wikivoyage 'South West (Western Australia)' Cities list and southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) (historic buildings, galleries, Bridgetown Art Trail, Christmas shop); a Blackwood Valley base.
objection: Best known for the Blues at Bridgetown festival, which is an event and does not count; town draws are modest (main street, galleries).

name: Manjimup
reason: Re-looked: southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) town page and 8-day itinerary (Manjimup Heritage Park, food bowl); regional hub of the Southern Forests (COVERAGE: sizable settlements/hubs are kept).
objection: Only one counted source family found; its best sights (Diamond Tree, King Jarrah, Heritage Park) are separate places.

name: Nannup
reason: Re-looked: southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) town page and itinerary (heritage trail of 51 sites, galleries, Tank 7 lookout, Blackwood River), and Wikivoyage Pemberton 'Go next'.
objection: Small village; one substantive counted source; draws are low-key (heritage walk, galleries).

name: Balingup
reason: Re-looked: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury Geographe page ('inspiration to artisans... one of WA's top tourist drives') and southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) (Golden Valley Tree Park, scarecrows, main street). Two counted sources.
objection: Tiny village; Golden Valley Tree Park is its main sight and may be its own spot.

name: Boyup Brook
reason: Re-looked: only southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) lists it, with generic text ('natural wonders, local artisans, local produce'); no named sight.
objection: Against: one counted source and nothing specific to see or do (brief: a town with nothing a source names is reject or review). For: a listed town of the regional board, gateway for country-music events (events do not count).

name: Northcliffe
reason: Re-looked: southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) town page and itinerary name the Understory Art & Nature Walk, the Pioneer Museum, Mount Chudalup and Windy Harbour nearby.
objection: For: gateway to D'Entrecasteaux NP and Windy Harbour with a named art trail and museum. Against: one counted source, and its named draws (Understory, Mount Chudalup) are separate candidates, so the town may be a wrapper.

name: Australind
reason: Re-looked: harveyregion.com.au (Shire of Harvey tourism) Australind page names the Australind Jetty, the Leschenault Waterways Eco Museum, the estuary crabbing and the heritage trail.
objection: Against: one local-government tourism source; a residential satellite of Bunbury ('Australia's fastest growing regional location') with cafes and a big pub; a traveller from elsewhere rarely goes out of their way for it. For: estuary jetty and eco museum.

name: Gracetown
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Margaret River names it for beaches and surf breaks; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Cowaramup & Gracetown town page (Cowaramup Bay, North Point, South Point, Huzza's) and Gracetown Beach page. Second-tier harbour/surf village.
objection: Small hamlet; its beach ('Gracetown Beach') is the same place, so keep one (town or beach), not both.

name: Prevelly
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Prevelly & Gnarabup' town page names the beaches, Margaret River Mouth, St John the Theologian Church, the Prevelly Sculpture Loop Walk and Surfers Point.
objection: Against: its headline draw is Surfers Point (kept separately), so the village is likely a wrapper or near-duplicate (COVERAGE: never list a town beside its own attraction). For: a named surf village with its own beaches and river mouth.

name: Hamelin Bay
reason: Rule 1-3: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Hamelin Bay Beach' ('a must-do... white sand, turquoise water, stingrays, shipwreck') and the australiassouthwest.com listing. Two counted sources.
objection: Wild stingrays are the main draw and not guaranteed; the village itself is a caravan park and boat ramp.

name: Cowaramup
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Cowaramup town page and '10 places you can't miss in Cowaramup': 42 life-size fibreglass cows (quirky roadside icon), cellar doors, chocolate and produce shops; Wikivoyage Margaret River 'Go next'.
objection: Mostly shops and cafés in a pass-through town on Bussell Highway; the cows are a short photo stop.

name: Busselton Underwater Observatory
reason: Rule 3: part of a larger spot. It is at the end of Busselton Jetty and is sold as part of the jetty visit (Wikivoyage Busselton lists it under the jetty); Busselton Jetty is kept and its bio covers the observatory.
objection: Separately ticketed and the jetty's best-known experience; could be argued as its own spot like a museum inside a precinct.

name: Wonnerup House
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Busselton See and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) (National Trust house, open Fri-Sat, visitors may explore the house and its interpretation); 1859 homestead with dairy, kitchen, school and teacher's house. Two counted sources.
objection: Open only two days a week, and the furnishings are in storage during reinterpretation, so the visit is thinner than it was.

name: Old Butter Factory and Busselton Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Busselton See and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) museum page (open Wed-Mon 10-4; display rooms on dairy, timber, maritime and Group Settlement history in the 1918 butter factory). Two counted sources.
objection: A local-history museum; a traveller would go only if already in Busselton.

name: St Mary's Church Busselton
reason: Church rule: Wikivoyage Busselton singles it out (built 1844-45, believed the oldest stone church in WA, graveyard with graves from 1841) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) page says visitors can wander the graveyard and read the settlers' tombstones.
objection: For: a landmark guides single out, with a graveyard to explore. Against: the board files it under 'local services', it is a working parish church mostly seen from outside, and the visit is about 15 minutes.

name: Busselton Visitor Centre and Railway Museum
reason: Rule 2-3: a visitor information centre (bookings, maps, souvenirs) beside Busselton Jetty; its railway display (the Ballaarat, WA's first steam locomotive, in Railway House) is a small exhibit in the jetty foreshore precinct, not a distinct draw.
objection: The Ballaarat locomotive is historically notable and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) gives it an article; could be a short stop on the Busselton foreshore.

name: Weld Hall Busselton
reason: Rule 2: a civic hall/community theatre (Weld Theatre), seen from the street; Wikivoyage describes only its exterior and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) lists it as a performance venue.
objection: 1881 Mechanics' Institute, one of the oldest buildings in Busselton.

name: Ithaca Busselton
reason: Rule 2: a heritage house now operating as a motel (accommodation); seen from the street only.
objection: Heritage-listed 1896 house with a tower, named by Wikivoyage.

name: Nglili Cave
reason: Duplicate of Ngilgi Cave (Wikivoyage Dunsborough misspells Ngilgi as 'Nglili'; same cave west of Dunsborough on Caves Road). Kept as one under Ngilgi Cave.
objection: None beyond the name; it is the same cave.

name: Meelup Regional Park
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Meelup Reserve' page (11.5 km of coast from Dunsborough to Bunker Bay, whale lookouts, beaches, wildflower walks) and its 'Biking and hiking at Meelup Regional Park' article; westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Dunsborough page names Meelup. Two counted sources.
objection: Meelup Beach is the draw and may be its own candidate; if both are kept they overlap (keep one, the beach or the park), and Eagle Bay, Castle Rock and Bunker Bay sit inside the park.

name: Eagle Bay
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Eagle Bay beach page (calm swimming beach, HMAS Swan dive wreck, Point Piquet) and westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Dunsborough page ('stop-and-stare breathtaking'). Second-tier beach a source names.
objection: Partly inside Meelup Regional Park; one of several similar calm Geographe Bay beaches.

name: Bunker Bay
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Bunker Bay beach page (sheltered beach near Cape Naturaliste, café, snorkelling) and westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Dunsborough page. Second-tier beach a source names.
objection: No coordinates in the candidate; overlaps the Cape Naturaliste walks (Bunker Bay loop) and is mostly known for its resort.

name: Koombana Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Bunbury See names it (protected beach on Koombana Bay where wild dolphins come close to shore); westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury text names Koombana Bay and shoreline dolphins.
objection: For: wild dolphins at the beach. Against: Wikivoyage calls it 'a modest beach', and the dolphin interaction zone and visitor facilities are the Dolphin Discovery Centre on the same beach, so it is a near-duplicate of that spot.

name: Dolphin Discovery Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Bunbury (aquariums, 360-degree digital dolphinarium, eco-cruises; daily) and the australiassouthwest.com listing; westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury text features the wild dolphins. Two counted sources.
objection: Wild dolphins are not guaranteed and the cruises are an operator product; the place is the centre and beach, which is what is kept.

name: Wardan Aboriginal Culture Centre
reason: Rule 2: not confirmed open. Wikivoyage Margaret River lists the name only; a museum directory lists it as temporarily closed, local news reported it might close and that bushfire risk had stopped its cultural use; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) no longer lists it.
objection: If it reopened, an Aboriginal cultural centre run by the Wadandi would be a strong draw; worth rechecking.

name: Margaret River School of Wine
reason: Brief: a business (wine education classes and tasting venue), not a place a source singles out as a destination; Wikivoyage names it only in a list.
objection: Offers a structured tasting a visitor could book.

name: Colonial Brewery
reason: Brief: a brewery-restaurant; Wikivoyage mentions it only as a lunch-and-playground suggestion in a sample day, not as a destination in its own right (the region has dozens of breweries).
objection: Family-friendly lunch stop with a playground.

name: Cape Leeuwin
reason: Wikivoyage Margaret River 'See' names Cape Leeuwin; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Edge of the world: the great Cape Leeuwin' (where two oceans meet, whales). Strong name (16k views).
objection: Not a separate place from Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse: visitors reach the cape at the lighthouse precinct (ticketed grounds, interpretive centre), which is listed separately by Wikivoyage and the board. Keep as ONE spot (the lighthouse, with 'where two oceans meet' in its bio) rather than both; review only to decide which name carries it.

name: Cape Naturaliste
reason: Wikivoyage Leeuwin-Naturaliste NP and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Cape Naturaliste' scenic-spot page (boardwalks, Whale Lookout walk, Cape Naturaliste loop, track to Sugarloaf Rock).
objection: Shares its car park and precinct with Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse, listed separately; the walks are short sections of the Cape to Cape Track. Keep as one with the lighthouse unless the owner wants the headland walks as their own spot.

name: Canal Rocks
reason: Rule 1-3: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Canal Rocks' (granite channel crossed by a timber walkway, rock pools, lookout; open 24 h) and the australiassouthwest.com listing. Two counted sources.
objection: A short stop (30 minutes) on the coast road near Yallingup.

name: Injidup Natural Spa
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Yallingup Do (natural rock pool, short hike from the car park) and the australiassouthwest.com listing. Two counted sources.
objection: Only a 'spa' at the right tide and swell, and dangerous in big seas; no coordinates in the candidate.

name: Yallingup Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Yallingup (swimming, surfing, the southernmost tropical fish reef for snorkelling) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Yallingup Beach & Rabbit Hill' (lagoon, surf break, lookout). Two counted sources.
objection: Overlaps the Yallingup town candidate (the beach is the town's draw); keep the beach or the town as the spot, not a wrapper. No coordinates in the candidate.

name: Smiths Beach
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Smiths Beach page (long white-sand beach, Supertubes surf break, the Aquarium snorkelling lagoon nearby). Second-tier beach a counted source names.
objection: One counted source; its coordinates are Yallingup's town point (Wikipedia redirects to Yallingup), so the pin must be resolved afresh.

name: Surfers Point
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Surfers Point page (Main Break, World Surf League event, sunset lawns, whale watching Jun-Dec) and westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Margaret River page names it as the WSL venue. Two counted sources.
objection: The WSL contest is an event and does not count; the place itself is a surf break and lookout, a 30-minute stop.

name: Redgate Beach
reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) Redgate Beach page (surf break, granite boulders, Georgette shipwreck and Grace Bussell story). Second-tier beach a counted source names.
objection: One counted source; unpatrolled surf beach with dangerous rips.

name: Ferguson Valley
reason: Re-looked: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Bunbury Geographe page: 'rolling hills, vineyards, casual microbreweries and the oddity of Gnomesville make this area a must-see'. A food-and-wine valley visitors travel for (COVERAGE: wine/food regions).
objection: An area rather than one place; Gnomesville and Wellington National Park are separate candidates, so the proposer must decide whether it is a destination or a spot.

name: Margaret River wine region
reason: Duplicate of Margaret River: Wikivoyage says 'Margaret River is now the common term for the region between the capes'; kept as one under the Margaret River candidate (proposer decides whether the destination is the town or the region).
objection: The wine region is the actual draw and has 6.9k views; if the destination is named for the region, this name should carry it instead.

name: Leeuwin Estate
reason: Brief winery rule met: a landmark founding estate singled out by margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) and the australiassouthwest.com listing, with an art gallery of the 'Art Series' collection (Olsen, Boyd, Nolan) open to visitors, cellar door daily. Two counted sources.
objection: Still a winery among 200+; its famous concerts are events and do not count.

name: Cape Mentelle Vineyards
reason: Board listing (australiassouthwest.com) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) winery page: founding winery (1970), twice Jimmy Watson trophy winner, cellar door daily, vineyard tours.
objection: For: a founding estate a board names. Against: a cellar door like dozens of others, with no visitor attraction beyond tasting; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination in its own right.

name: Vasse Felix
reason: Brief winery rule met: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Margaret River page names it among the heritage winemakers, margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) calls it Margaret River's founding wine estate with a wine museum and art gallery (Holmes a Court Collection), and the australiassouthwest.com listing. Three counted sources.
objection: A winery and restaurant; the gallery is the non-tasting draw.

name: Moss Wood
reason: Rule 2: not open to the public; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) says visits are 'by appointment only', 'a privilege of Moss Wood membership', with a $100 charge. Tourism WA names it among heritage winemakers, but a walk-in visitor cannot go.
objection: A founding estate named by Tourism WA; members can book a guided visit.

name: Devil's Lair Winery
reason: Rule 1-2: no counted source found (margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) sitemap and Tourism WA pages do not name it); a wine brand with no public cellar door listed.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article (849 views).

name: Voyager Estate
reason: Board listing (australiassouthwest.com) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) page: family estate in the Stevens Valley with a wine room, private tours and an award-winning restaurant (Regional Restaurant of the Year 2025).
objection: For: a well-known estate with tours. Against: tastings and dining only; no source read singles it out as a destination beyond the cellar door (brief winery rule).

name: Cullen Wines
reason: Re-looked: westernaustralia.com (Tourism WA) Margaret River page names Cullen among the heritage winemakers; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) page (the only biodynamic, carbon-positive winery in the region, wine room open daily).
objection: For: two counted sources, a pioneer estate. Against: a cellar door and restaurant like many others; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination.

name: Calgardup Cave
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Leeuwin-Naturaliste NP (self-guided 300 m cave with a stream, park visitor centre, daily 9-4:15) and DBCA Explore Parks caving page ('self-guided tours in Calgardup Cave... suitable for all ages, most days'). Two counted sources.
objection: Less famous than Jewel, Lake, Mammoth and Ngilgi; a short self-guided visit.

name: Giants Cave
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Leeuwin-Naturaliste NP and DBCA Explore Parks 'Giants Cave' page (86 m deep, ladders and scrambles, self-guided one-hour adventure caving, minimum age 6). Two counted sources.
objection: Open only some months (closed May-Sep except school holidays): a seasonal venue, which still counts.

name: Jewel Cave
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Leeuwin-Naturaliste NP (world's longest straw stalactite in a show cave) and the australiassouthwest.com listing; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) lists it among the Margaret River caves. Obvious draw.
objection: None significant; one of four commercial show caves.

name: Moondyne Cave
reason: Rule 2 / brief (closed places are rejected): Wikipedia says Moondyne Cave is not currently open for tours; Wikivoyage lists the name with no details, and neither margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) nor DBCA offers it.
objection: An old showcaves listing gives weekend tours June-December (2023); if tours resume it would qualify.

name: Yourdamung Lake
reason: Rule 1: no counted source (Wikipedia only); a local lake and reserve. Note: the candidate's coordinates (-33.09, 116.33) are inland near Collie, not 'in Augusta' as its note says.
objection: None found.

name: Town Beach Augusta
reason: Rule 1/3: no counted source names it (Wikipedia Augusta only); a local town beach below Augusta, not a distinct draw.
objection: Sheltered swimming spot in a town that is kept.

name: Wadandi Track
reason: Rule 1: the Shire of Augusta Margaret River (managing authority) trail page names it: a walk/cycle rail trail on the former Busselton–Flinders Bay railway, 46 km open in two sections (Busselton Jetty–Carbunup River, Cowaramup–Sebbes Road), being completed to 109 km by 2028. Rule 2 met (walk or ride it).
objection: Only one counted source and that is a council page, not a tourism or guide listing; the trail is incomplete until 2028 and the note placed it 'around Augusta', whereas the open sections are Busselton and Cowaramup; may be better added once finished. Case for: state-funded flagship trail the region is promoting.

name: Boranup Forest
reason: Rules 1-3: Australia's South West board listing plus the DBCA Leeuwin-Naturaliste page for Boranup Forest (Boranup Drive through westernmost karri forest, Boranup Lookout, campground, picnic area); a distinct forest drive and lookout off Caves Road, free entry.
objection: It is part of Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park; if the park itself is a spot the forest could read as a sub-part. But the guides treat it as its own named stop.

name: Gloucester Tree
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Pemberton (Do: 'maybe the most popular' lookout tree) and DBCA's Gloucester Tree page; a 1947 fire-lookout karri with climbing pegs to a 37 m (lookout) platform, plus picnic area and forest walks. Obvious draw, 8,442 page views.
objection: DBCA notes a South West Climbing Trees Project to upgrade platforms and reopen the trees to climbing, so climbing may be intermittently closed; the tree, walks and picnic area remain open whatever.

name: Diamond Tree
reason: Rule 2: DBCA says the Diamond Tree is 'now permanently CLOSED for climbing' (rot in the base, 2019); what is left is a picnic area and short walk at a roadside tree. Its draw (climbing) is closed and Wikivoyage's listing is out of date.
objection: Still a historic 1940 lookout tree with a picnic stop and walk, 2,500 page views; could be a 15-minute roadside look. Not a distinct draw once the climb is gone.

name: Beedelup Falls
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Pemberton (See) and Australia's South West board listing, and DBCA's Greater Beedelup NP page ('Don't miss Beedelup Falls'): falls, boardwalk and suspension bridge, the Walk-Through Tree on the 4.5 km loop.
objection: Falls are seasonal (best in winter and spring) and the boardwalk area is a short visit; but two counted sources and the loop walk make it a full stop.

name: Pemberton Tramway
reason: A spot is a place, not the way you get there: the Pemberton Tramway Company is an operator's tram ride; the karri forest it runs through is covered by Gloucester Tree / Warren National Park.
objection: Wikivoyage and the board list it, and a heritage tram could be 'the ride is the attraction' (COVERAGE exception); but it runs to the Warren River bridge forest, not a distinct named place, and the forest is listed separately. Mention in the Pemberton description or a spot bio.

name: Karri Forest Explorer
reason: Rule 3: an 86 km drive route that links places judged on their own (Gloucester Tree, Beedelup Falls, Warren National Park and its Bicentennial Tree); it is the way between those spots, not a distinct place.
objection: DBCA promotes it as a named touring drive and visitors do plan around it; the owner may prefer it as a route spot. Its content is already carried by the parks and trees it links.

name: Heartbreak Trail
reason: Rule 3: a one-way drive inside Warren National Park (DBCA Warren page: 'drive the Heartbreak Trail or the Karri Forest Explorer'); part of a larger spot.
objection: It is the park's signature drive down to the Warren River; if Warren National Park were rejected it would be the place to keep instead.

name: Great Forest Trees Drive
reason: Rule 3: the 50 km drive is part of Shannon National Park (DBCA Shannon page), which is kept as the spot; the drive goes in its bio.
objection: It is the main thing visitors do in Shannon; an owner could prefer the drive's name over the park's.

name: Snake Gully Lookout
reason: Rule 3: a lookout inside Shannon National Park (DBCA names it with Big Tree Grove as a top spot in the park); part of a larger spot, kept via the park.
objection: DBCA singles it out by name; could be a sub-spot if the park ends up a destination of its own.

name: Big Tree Grove
reason: Rule 3: a grove on a walk inside Shannon National Park; part of the park, kept via Shannon National Park. (Its Wikipedia title is a California grove, so it also lacks a stable reference.)
objection: DBCA names it as one of the best places to see 90 m karri; could be a sub-spot of a Shannon destination.

name: King Jarrah Heritage Trail
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA 'King Jarrah' park page and Trails WA (state trails site): a 45 m, roughly 500-year-old jarrah saved from sleeper cutters, with a 600 m sealed path, picnic area and BBQs, 4.5 km from Manjimup; free. Second-tier stop two counted sources name. Name it 'King Jarrah' (the sources' name); there is no Wikipedia article at this title, and a different 'King Jarrah Heritage Trail' exists in Lane Poole Reserve near Dwellingup (Peel, closed after fire), so do not take coordinates or photos from that one.
objection: Short visit (about 30 min) at a single tree on the edge of town; arguably a local picnic reserve.

name: Shannon National Park
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA Shannon NP page: old-growth karri, the 50 km Great Forest Trees Drive, Snake Gully Lookout, Big Tree Grove, Mokare's Rock boardwalk, Shannon Dam walk, campground and horse camp. Visitor source names plenty to do; holds the drive, lookout and grove candidates.
objection: Only one counted source (the agency's own page) and 706 views; a quieter park than Warren or Gloucester.

name: Warren National Park
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA Warren NP page and Wikivoyage Pemberton (Dave Evans Bicentennial Tree, 'excellent campgrounds'): karri forest, the Bicentennial Tree climb, Heartbreak Trail drive, Warren River canoeing and two campgrounds.
objection: The Dave Evans Bicentennial Tree is its headline; if the tree is listed separately, the park could be a near-duplicate. The Bicentennial Tree is not in this shard, so the park carries it here.

name: Greater Beedelup National Park
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Beedelup Falls: DBCA's park page is about the falls, the Walk-Through Tree and the loop walk between them, which the Beedelup Falls spot covers.
objection: The park has its own DBCA page and the Karri Forest Explorer passes through; owner could prefer the park name with the falls as its bio.

name: Gloucester National Park
reason: DBCA page: karri forest walks (Gloucester Tree–Cascades 12 km, 10 km loop, Pemberton town link), mountain biking, the Cascades rapids on Lefroy Brook, Aerial Adventure Pemberton. More than the tree alone.
objection: Near-duplicate of the Gloucester Tree, which is what visitors come for and which sits in it; one counted source (the agency's own page). Keep only if the Cascades/trails are not carried by the tree spot.
